source.title: Beyond Single-Value Metrics: Evaluating and Enhancing LLM Unlearning with Cognitive Diagnosis
source.authors: Yi-Cheng Lang; Ke-Han Guo; Yue Huang; Yu-Jun Zhou; Hao-Min Zhuang; Tian-Yu Yang; Yao Su; Xiang-Liang Zhang

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates the effect of several unlearning methods on targeted cyber-knowledge performance and general capability using its own benchmark. It does not test recovery attacks.
record.gate_note: The authors report unlearning outcomes and capability-retention metrics for eight methods on two models. They discuss residual knowledge concepts and show further unlearning by UNCD-Agent, but do not apply fine-tuning recovery attacks, activation ablation, quantization, or prompt-only recovery. No result is reported for those attacks. Figure-based knowledge-state details are not transcribed as numeric results here.
record.test_reason: It runs eight published unlearning methods (including RMU from WMDP) on Llama-3-8B and Mistral-7B and reports cyber-knowledge QA accuracy against 25% chance alongside MMLU, in-domain and fluency retention. That tests version A's first two parts. It also argues that aggregate accuracy near chance hides residual knowledge concepts, which says A needs restating. It runs no recovery attack, so B–F and A's attack clause are untested.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that single-value QA accuracy can give a false sense of unlearning success because concept-level knowledge persists. Cognitive diagnosis exposes those remnants, and UNCD-Agent's targeted data reduces them with slight utility loss. They do not claim the knowledge is recoverable by attacks.
record.recipe_differences: The study applies published unlearning methods to a cyberattack forget set and measures forgetting and retained ability. It does not run any of the recovery attacks in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes differ by unlearning method and base model; the paper reports markedly different forget and retain performance across methods and between Llama-3-8B and Mistral-7B.

fits_no_version.finding: Models whose aggregate forget accuracy looks successful still keep specific knowledge concepts. Examples: Llama GAGDR keeps 'collection'; GA/NPO keep 'defense-evasion' and 'reconnaissance' (Fig. 1, Fig. 3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Aggregate forget-set accuracy near chance can mask concept-level residual knowledge after unlearning.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: Only two base models and a cybersecurity-specific generated evaluation benchmark are used. The study does not test recovery attacks, so it cannot determine whether the reported residual knowledge can be recovered by the attacks in the claim. Table 2 does not state uncertainty for its QA or MMLU values, although confidence intervals are reported for knowledge-state measures in Table 4.

untested.parts: Whether simple attacks recover the knowledge; no attack is run.
All; no activation ablation or internal analysis.
All; no rephrasing, jailbreak, language or in-context attack.
All; UNCD-Agent is further unlearning and is not tested against attacks.

missing.what: In-domain retain accuracy (UNCD-Cyber retain set) and MT-Bench fluency per method. These show utility loss even where MMLU holds, e.g. Llama GAGDR in-domain 57.19→30.17 and fluency 5.62→3.97.
missing.locator: Table 2, In-Domain Acc. and Fluency columns

missing.what: Concept-level residual knowledge despite low aggregate accuracy (figure only).

record.verdict_notes: Table 4 does not match Table 2 for Llama RMU/TV NCDM values (67.43/68.71 vs 55.43/53.98) or Mistral RMU (52.37 vs 49.17). Mistral NPO's ICDM CI does not match its mean. Ms metrics are the study's own method and are rightly not rows. The record's supports label was wrong: it cited r21/r23, whose paired forget accuracies are 50.10 and 58.68. No method on either model met both parts of A cleanly.

versions.untested_parts: The study measures targeted performance and general capability after unlearning, but does not test whether attacks recover knowledge.
No post-unlearning recovery fine-tuning on unrelated, loosely related, or forgotten-fact examples.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis establishing access-blocking rather than deletion.
No prompt rephrasing, jailbreak, language, or in-context recovery attack.
UNCD-Agent performs further targeted unlearning; the study does not test resistance to the attacks listed in the claim.

relationships.reason: Forget accuracy is near chance (r2 16.81, r13 27.24). MMLU is kept for Llama (r18 59.84) but only partly for Mistral (r29 42.81). Per Table 2, Llama GAGDR in-domain accuracy falls 57.19→30.17, and per the text residual 'collection' knowledge remains.
relationships.display_finding: Forget accuracy reached 16.81 on Llama and 27.24 on Mistral, with MMLU at 59.84/42.81; Llama in-domain accuracy fell from 57.19 to 30.17 and collection knowledge persisted.

relation.reason: Its own forgetting and MMLU/in-domain retention results bear on version A.

tranche.reason: Runs published methods and argues near-chance QA accuracy gives a 'false sense of unlearning success' because concept-level knowledge remains. That bears on whether version A needs restating. T2 is defensible too. No recovery attacks are run.

source_check.notes: No recovery attacks are run, so only the first two parts of version A are tested. Methods ran for one epoch with MUSE settings; RMU used WMDP's Zephyr-7B config, untuned here. Table 2 is flattened; cells were placed by column order (Acc, 3 Ms, In-Domain, General, Fluency).

statements.correction: This study: UNCD-Cyber (GPT-4o-generated from MITRE ATT&CK), Llama-3-8B MMLU 62.19 -> 28.56 (GA), 22.95 (NPO); forget Acc 61.96 -> 13.86 (GA), 29.75 (NPO) (Table 2).
